data.body:
=== TRIAGE: the INBOUND LINK cell — ROOT CAUSE PROVEN, AND IT IS NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT. It is a
single-pass ordering constraint, and the cell that failed is NOT the cell now on main. ===

FIRST, THE THING THAT REFRAMES IT. The observed failure — "the inbound Jira link did not surface
as a local dep on jira-rbjjsuj-1: deps target [], expected to contain 'jira-rbjjsuj-2'" (run
30731818113, job 91453401952) — was produced by the PRE-PRIMING version of the cell. The failing
source is in the log verbatim: `set_relationship` follows `other_local = _jira_key_to_local_id(...)`
with NO pass in between. `git show 338e397335:tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`
confirms the priming pass was absent at the commit that run tested. It was added by
**ae009443a9** (ticket b9b8), which landed AFTER that run. So the STATUS UPDATE's "still unowned"
entry describes a cell that has since been changed, and no harness run has exercised the current
one.

THE MECHANISM, verified rather than assumed. The inbound link translator drops a link in two
independent situations, both of which hold on the pass that FIRST sees the link target:
  * `inbound_differ.py:402-404` — `binding_store.get_local_id(other_key)` is falsy -> `continue`
    ("unbound — retry next pass"). A DC issue the pass is about to import has no binding yet.
  * `inbound_differ.py:409-412` — the counterpart is absent from `local_tickets_by_id` -> `continue`
    ("don't mirror to a dormant ticket"). That dict is `local_by_id` in
    `run_differs.py:_run_differs_inbound`, built from `ctx.local_tickets`, which
    **`reconcile.py:250` reads ONCE at pass start**, before anything is applied.
Both are unreachable within one pass because of the phase ORDER in `run_differs.run_differs`:
the inbound differ runs at `:239` and the binding walk that would adopt the new key at `:240`,
and `applier.apply` is not called until `reconcile.py:454`. Nothing gets bound or created
locally until every differ has already run.
Neither skip emits an alert or a log line, which is why the failure presents as an empty `deps`
rather than as a diagnosable message.

CONTROLLED REPRODUCTION, ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME —
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_lands_locally_5200.py` (6 tests, all
green, no live Jira). The same `_diff_links_inbound` call is made four times against a real
`Blocks` issuelink payload, changing exactly one input each time:
  * counterpart BOUND + PRESENT      -> `[{"action":"add","target_id":"local-b","relation":"blocks"}]`
  * counterpart UNBOUND only          -> `[]`
  * counterpart bound, LOCALLY ABSENT -> `[]`
  * the far-end MIRROR entry          -> `[{"action":"add","target_id":"local-a","relation":"depends_on"}]`
The positive case is what makes the two empty results evidence: the function is not simply
returning `[]` for everything.

AND THE REST OF THE PATH IS FINE, which is the part that had to be checked before filing
anything. Driven against a REAL initialised store in a temp dir:
  * `_inbound_update_apply_links` (`apply_inbound_records.py:527-560`) applies the differ's add
    through `rebar.link` and reports 1 applied;
  * the dep then reads back on `rebar.show_ticket(source)["deps"]` with `target_id` == the
    target — the EXACT projection the live oracle inspects;
  * applying BOTH mirror entries of one Jira link (which a real pass does, since both endpoints
    are in the snapshot) does not destroy the first edge — so `blocks(a,b)` + `depends_on(b,a)`
    is survivable and is not a hidden second cause.
Differ, applier and projection all work. There is NO product defect here and NO bug to file.

TWO UPSTREAM SUSPECTS I CHECKED AND REJECTED, recorded so the next session does not re-walk them:
  * `get_issuelinks_map` PAGINATION/FIELDS (9263). `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:404-407`
    calls `_paged_search(f"project = {project_key}", rate_limit_retry=True)` with `fields=None`.
    I suspected `fields=None` meant "no fields", which would have made the map `{key: []}` for
    every issue and then `fetcher.py:589-591` would OVERWRITE the base snapshot's real
    issuelinks with `[]`. **Wrong**: pycontribs `jira/client.py:3619-3620` converts `fields=None`
    to `["*all"]`, which includes issuelinks. The mapping is correct.
  * OUTBOUND LINK-REMOVE SUPPRESSION. `inbound_differ.py:672-690` drops an inbound link-ADD when
    the same pass's outbound is link-REMOVING the same key. It cannot fire here:
    `outbound_links._diff_link_removals` only emits a REMOVE for a link we MANAGED, and a link
    created directly in DC is never-managed and "left for inbound ADOPT, never clobbered"
    (`outbound_links.py:112-116`).

ALSO NOTED, NOT A CAUSE: the harness log carries `WARNING jira:client.py:3002 Warning: Specified
issue link type is not present in the list of link types` from the cell's own
`set_relationship`. It is spurious — `jira/client.py:3000` tests a `str` for membership in a
list of `IssueLinkType` RESOURCES, so it warns on EVERY call — and it does not change the
submitted type. Worth knowing because it looks alarming in the log and is not.

WHAT REMAINS TO VERIFY (stated as unverified rather than assumed): that the PRIMED cell now goes
green live. The setup assertions ae009443a9 added make its failure self-classifying — a failure
naming "SETUP FAILED: the link target is not bound" or "bound but not in the ACTIVE local set"
is the priming pass not doing its job, and only a failure PAST those two is a bridge finding.
